Good — the primary MS concept is **374919** ("Multiple sclerosis"). Now let me compute prevalence from our EHR database.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.person_id) AS total_population,
       SUM(CASE WHEN co.condition_concept_id = 374919 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ms_cases
FROM omop.person p
LEFT JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON p.person_id = co.person_id
WHERE p.year_of_birth <= YEAR(GETDATE()) - 18

content.text:
From the query results:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Adult population (≥18 y) | 6,452,146 |
| MS condition-occurrence records (concept_id 374919) | 665,148 |

However, the **665,148** count above is a row-level `condition_occurrence` count — any patient with multiple visits recorded for MS will be counted more than once. Let me correct that to get true prevalence:

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.person_id) AS total_population,
       (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT co2.person_id) FROM omop.condition_occurrence co2 WHERE co2.condition_concept_id = 374919 AND co2.person_id IN (SELECT person_id FROM omop.person WHERE year_of_birth <= YEAR(GETDATE()) - 18)) AS ms_cases
FROM omop.person p
WHERE p.year_of_birth <= YEAR(GETDATE()) - 18

content.text: That looks low given known epidemiology (MS affects roughly 1/700–1/1000 globally). Let me verify our cohort and check for a broader concept set — many patients might be coded under MS-related subtypes or synonyms.

arguments.sql_query: SELECT TOP 20 * FROM omop.concept WHERE concept_id = 374919

From your clinical records:

### Notes on accuracy

- 13,209 is a conservative count from the primary SNOMED concept for "Multiple sclerosis" (code `24700007`). Patients with subtype diagnoses (relapsing-remitting, progressive secondary/primary) may be underrepresented if coded under separate concepts.
- I can expand this to an MS concept set (parent + children/subtypes from the OMOP hierarchy) if you need a broader prevalence estimate or want it broken down by demographics (age group, sex).
